Great coffee brewer. - Where do I start. The aeropress is an amazing piece of equipment. Anyone who is looking for a really great cup of coffee, that tastes amazing and has a low impact on the environment then this is for you. You have the single serve convenience of a keurig, yet not all the wastefulness of the k-cups and all the packaging. Especially if you get yourself the "Able Brewing Disk" (do yourself a favor and buy them both at once). The idea of purchasing a manual coffee maker such as this may seem a little daunting, but after about a week of using it you won't even notice the slight bit of extra work you have to put into making your morning coffee. And trust me, the enhancement in flavor over anything you have brewed with in the past will blow you away, and make up for the little extra work you have to do. Not only is this a genius solution for making yourself a single cup of coffee with out wasting an entire pot, but it's a great solution for making a delicious iced coffee. Just brew it directly into a cup of ice, the heat from the brewing coffee will melt the ice and you will have a perfectly balanced cup of iced coffee. So if you want a great cup of coffee without leaving your house, this is the simplest solution.

Made in China. It's nice as long as you have the right expectations. - I’ve used a couple of these icemakers. There are quite a few of them being sold by different Chinese companies on Amazon right now. They may look slightly different, but they all operate the same. As long as you have proper expectations, they work fairly well.

The listing shows that this icemaker can make 27 pounds of ice per day. That would only be the case if someone empties the ice basket each and every time that it is full. It takes about an hour for it to feel, so you would have to have someone to constantly empty it, which is probably not going to happen.

This icemaker makes 9 cubes of ice at a time. They then empty into the holding basket which is on top of the water reservoir. Once the basket is full, it will stop making ice. If you do not remove the ice than the eye simply melts back down into the water reservoir, and the process starts all over again. You can remove the ice cubes and place them in a freezer, but the ice cubes are wet so when you place the cubes into the freezer they will freeze together in a clump. OK, not great - I bought the induction cooktop while it was on sale, just to try it out (after seeing demos on Cook's Illustrated). The biggest concern with all induction cooktops is that you must have the right cookware, but here I wanted to focus on what may be unique to this cooktop (versus others you might get).

PROS: Very fast at bringing pots and pans to temperature (for example, I can boil water in about 2 minutes using this cooktop, and it takes about 5 minutes on my electric stove), and fast at temperature control. There are also some nice safety features.

CONS: This does not have a continuous temp control, but 6 temps- I found that many times I need a slow simmer, but one temp was too high, and the next one down was too low. Another issue with low temps is that there is not a continuous low temp- The temperature pulses on and off. One annoyance (common or not?) is that when you lift a pan off the cooktop, it automatically gives a warning and shuts off.

Conclusions for me: Nice for occasional use, but not a complete replacement for electric or gas.
